source.filename: 2021_Bio-Inspired Soft Grippers Based on Impactive Gripping.pdf

actuation: biological contractile tissue (insect dorsal vessel tissue)
constitutive_assumptions: Biological soft tissues and elastomer matrices (PDMS, silicone rubber, Ecoflex) exhibit compliant, hyperelastic behavior with Young's moduli on the order of 10^2 to 10^6 Pa.

Muscular hydrostat organs (e.g., octopus tentacles, elephant trunks) maintain constant internal volume during muscle contraction, causing axial extension when radial dimensions decrease and vice versa.
Structural asymmetry (eccentric chamber placement, multi-material stiffness disparity, or corrugated walls) induces macroscopic bending or helical twisting under homogeneous pressure or contraction.
Shape memory alloys undergo reversible, diffusionless phase transformations between low-temperature martensite and high-temperature austenite crystalline phases.
Shape memory polymers exhibit dramatic reversible modulus drops across their glass transition temperature from a glassy state (gigapascal scale) to a rubbery state (megapascal scale).
Jamming mechanisms assume dry Coulomb or viscous friction between internal granules, sheets, or tubules that transition from a fluid-like state to a solid-like state under differential pressure.
control_variables: Cooling method and cooling rate (passive ambient cooling vs. active air/fan cooling or fluidic water microchannels)
Supply pressure limits and vacuum levels applied to pneumatic chambers and jamming envelopes
Maximum allowable driving voltages and electric field limits to avoid dielectric breakdown in DEAs
Geometrical dimensions and aspect ratios of pneumatic chambers and smart material strips
Target object properties (mass, rigidity, geometry, and surface fragility) during comparative grasping evaluations
dependent_variables: Output grasping force, tip blocked force, and pull-out force
Deformation stroke, bending angle, contraction ratio, and 3D spatial workspace
Actuation response time and cycle frequency
Stiffness variation ratio and elastic modulus range
Grasping success rate, shape adaptability, and object holding stability

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Impactive soft grippers can be categorized based on biological movement modes into non-continuum bending-type (NBG, ~21%), continuum bending-type (CBG, ~46%), and continuum twisting-type (CTG, ~33%).

Compliant matrix materials such as silicone elastomers, PDMS, and rubbers possess Young's moduli in the range of 10^2 to 10^6 Pa, comparable to human skin and muscular tissue to guarantee safe physical interaction.
Soft pneumatic actuators provide robust, high output force (e.g., blocked forces up to 77.36 N at 300 kPa) but exhibit significant nonlinearity due to gas compressibility.
Cable-driven non-continuum bending grippers combine elastic hinges with low-stretch tendons, achieving high stability, precise kinematics, and payload capacities exceeding 20 kg.

Granular, layer, and tubular jamming switch from liquid-like compliance to solid-like rigidity via differential pressure-induced friction, offering modulus variations from 2 to 100 MPa within 0.1 to 1.1 s.

Electrorheological and magnetorheological fluids achieve millisecond-range switching (10 to 170 ms), though ER requires 1 to 5 kV activation voltages and MR yields low solidification hardness (4.73 to 62.04 kPa).

Low-melting-point materials modulate structural modulus over an expansive range (0.0952 to 860 MPa) via thermal phase transitions, but require over 60 s to cool unless integrated with active water cooling.

Shape memory polymers can increase structural stiffness up to 120-fold (0.01 to 3 GPa) across their glass transition, enabling soft fingers to lift 1.5 kg payloads when coupled with fluidic cooling microchannels.

Dielectric elastomer actuators achieve rapid responses (>2000 Hz) and area expansions exceeding 300%, but require extreme electric fields (~150 MV/m) that risk dielectric breakdown unless liquid-dielectric self-healing designs are employed.

Ionic polymer metal composites operate at low driving voltages (1 to 5 V) with force density sufficient to lift 40 times their weight, but generate minimal absolute force (e.g., 36 mN at 7 V), restricting them to micro-gripping.

experimental_setup: Mechanical tensile and load-cell testing benches for measuring fingertip blocked forces, pulling forces, and load-holding capacities
High-speed camera and optical tracking systems to quantify bending angles, elongation, and transient response times under cyclic excitation
Active thermal management setups including cooling fans, ice/cold water baths, and integrated fluidic microchannels for thermal actuator cooling
Environmental test chambers for aquatic specimen collection (e.g., live jellyfish and goldfish handling), deep-sea high-pressure simulation chambers, and open-air ambient humidity testing
Electromagnetic excitation coils, high-voltage amplifiers, and pneumatic control manifolds with vacuum pumps and positive pressure regulators
future_work: Developing soft actuators with high energy conversion efficiency, rapid response times, high output forces, and precise positioning capabilities
Realizing multi-axis, controllable twisting motions in compact continuum grippers without adding bulky or complex control infrastructure
Integrating untethered non-contact heating mechanisms (such as high-frequency magnetothermal or induction heating) and embedded fluidic cooling microchannels to accelerate thermal response cycles
Lowering activation voltages of electroactive polymers and electrorheological fluids to intrinsically safe levels while preventing dielectric breakdown and aging
Combining impactive grasping mechanisms with switchable adhesion (suction cups, gecko-like dry adhesion, electroadhesion, or capillary adhesion) for improved grasping of smooth surfaces
Engineering resilient materials (such as anti-freezing organohydrogels) to endure extreme temperature, pressure, and corrosive environments (deep sea, space, polar regions)
Integrating multi-modal flexible sensor skins capable of detecting temperature, moisture, texture, and roughness to enable bio-inspired adaptive responses
independent_variables: Actuation pressure or vacuum level applied to fluidic and jamming chambers
Tendon displacement, pulling force, and pulling speed in cable transmissions
Magnitude and frequency of applied electric voltage/field in DEAs, IPMCs, and ER fluids
Electric current and heating duration for Joule heating in SMAs, SMPs, and LMPAs
Magnetic field strength, flux density, or permanent magnet displacement in MR fluids and magnetic SMPs
Environmental stimuli including optical wavelength/power, solution pH, salinity, and ambient humidity
Structural geometry parameters (asymmetry layout, channel orientation, fiber winding angle, and layer thickness)
limitations_inferred: As a comprehensive literature review, quantitative metrics reported across cited studies were derived under non-standardized testing procedures, disparate specimen geometries, and varying load definitions, limiting direct cross-study equivalency.

The presented biological analogies, while useful for macroscopic classification, inherently abstract away the complex neuromuscular control and tribological skin adaptations present in living organisms.

Most surveyed variable-stiffness prototypes remain tethered to bulky auxiliary equipment (pumps, compressors, high-voltage transformers, power supplies), which offsets the practical autonomy of soft robotic systems.
limitations_stated_by_authors: CTGs require complicated structural architectures and control algorithms to achieve twisting motions, and most conventional soft actuators only generate planar bending.
Stimuli-responsive smart materials and SMPs exhibit low recovery stress and limited output force, restricting them primarily to low-load laboratory demonstrations.

Thermal responsive materials (SMAs, SMPs, LMPAs) suffer from slow passive cooling rates (>60 s to several minutes), severely restricting their actuation frequency unless bulky cooling units are added.
Dielectric elastomer actuators require dangerously high operating voltages (up to 150 MV/m or multiple kilovolts), posing human safety hazards and causing electrical aging or dielectric breakdown.
Electrorheological fluids require high voltages (1 to 5 kV), while magnetorheological fluids suffer from low solidified yield stress and high density.

Soft elastomer bodies and hydrogels degrade, dehydrate, or tear in harsh environments (extreme temperatures, pressures, or corrosive conditions), leading to rapid failure without specialized protective measures.

Existing soft grippers possess insufficient perceptual capabilities, being largely restricted to basic strain or contact pressure rather than multi-modal tactile sensing (temperature, moisture, roughness).
main_results: Established a biologically-inspired classification dividing impactive soft grippers into non-continuum bending-type (NBG), continuum bending-type (CBG), and continuum twisting-type (CTG), noting that CBGs dominate literature (~46%) due to structural simplicity, whereas nature favors NBGs and CTGs.

Provided a comprehensive performance and mechanism breakdown across eight soft actuation technologies: SPAs, cable-driven tendons, SMAs, SMPs, DEAs, IPMCs, LCEs, and other stimuli-responsive smart materials.

Surveyed five major variable-stiffness strategies (jamming effects, electrorheological fluids, magnetorheological fluids, low-melting materials, and shape memory materials), detailing their physical principles, modulus variations, response times, and trade-offs between low-stiffness adaptability and high-stiffness load capacity.

Identified persistent functional trade-offs across soft grippers, notably between compliance/adaptability and payload capacity, actuation speed and cooling duration, and driving power and electrical/mechanical safety.
modeling_methods: Biologically-inspired kinematic movement-mode classification framework (NBG, CBG, CTG)
Geometrically exact steady-state continuum mechanics modeling (cited from Renda et al. for octopus-inspired manipulators)
Inverse statics modeling and supervised learning algorithms for cable-driven continuum arms (cited from literature)
Finite element analysis (FEA) for cross-sectional geometry optimization of elastomeric pneumatic chambers (cited from Elsayed et al.)
Analytical constitutive models predicting bending angles and output forces of shape memory alloy strips (cited from She et al.)
performance_metrics: Response time and cycle frequency (s, ms, Hz)
Gripper size and length (cm, mm, µm)
Maximum load capacity and lifting payload (g, kg, N)
Actuation / blocked / gripping / fingertip force (N, mN, µN)
Bending angle (degrees) and contraction/elongation strain ratio (%)
Range of modulus variation and stiffness enhancement ratio (MPa, GPa, fold-change)
Actuation area expansion (%) and power density (kW/kg)
possible_gap_implications: While variable-stiffness mechanisms (jamming, LMPAs, SMPs) significantly enhance payload capacities in bending grippers, integrating them into high-DOF continuum twisting grippers without adding excessive rigid mass or tethering remains an unaddressed research gap.

The extended recovery latency of thermally responsive variable-stiffness elements indicates an engineering gap for localized, high-rate microscale active cooling and untethered electromagnetic induction heating.

The safety risks and breakdown vulnerability associated with kilovolt-level dielectric elastomers highlight a material development gap for high-permittivity, low-voltage electroactive polymers suitable for human-interactive soft robotics.

The absence of integrated multi-modal sensory feedback (thermal, moisture, roughness) in current impactive soft grippers creates an autonomy gap for closed-loop grasping of delicate, unknown objects in unstructured settings.
paper.research_objective: To provide an exhaustive, updated review of the research progress on bio-inspired impactive soft grippers, establish a novel classification system based on biological movement modes (non-continuum bending, continuum bending, continuum twisting), evaluate diverse soft actuation methods and variable-stiffness strategies, and identify persistent engineering challenges and future development directions.
paper.research_problem: Traditional rigid robotic grippers possess high structural stiffness that limits elastic adaptability to target geometries and poses safety hazards during human-robot or delicate-object interactions; conversely, soft grippers offer compliance and safety but suffer from low load capacity, limited precision, and lack a unified biologically-inspired classification and comprehensive evaluation of stiffness-controllable mechanisms.
paper.robot_type: soft grippers (classified into non-continuum bending-type grippers, continuum bending-type grippers, and continuum twisting-type grippers; including soft manipulators and bionic hands)
stiffness_mechanism: jamming effect (granular jamming, layer jamming, tubular jamming)
low-melting materials (low-melting-point alloys / LMPAs, conductive polylactic acid / CPLA, conductive propylene-based elastomer-PDMS composites)
shape memory materials (shape memory polymers / SMPs, shape memory alloys / SMAs)
paper.title: Bio-Inspired Soft Grippers Based on Impactive Gripping
